Administration.title: Administration
Administration.description: multi-administratie (design.md D2): the accountant multi-client tenant catalog -- ONE row per client administratie. This is the switcher's source list and the topbar/Dashboard indicator's label source; child HR/payroll objects do NOT $ref this schema (ADR-062 rule 7 -- they carry a plain-string copy of `administrationId` instead, D1). `administrationId` is the stable business key already used fleet-wide as a plain string on the payroll aggregates (PayrollRun/PayrollMutationReport/PayrollGLPost/PayrollPaymentBatch); this schema is where that key finally becomes a real, addressable catalog entry.

administrationId.description: The stable business key every other HR/payroll schema's denormalized administrationId property names (REQ-MULTI-001) -- e.g. 'ADM-001'. Unique per administratie; NOT the OpenRegister object id/UUID.

name.description: Display name of the client administratie (e.g. 'Voorbeeld Accountancy B.V.'). The switcher's option label and the topbar/Dashboard indicator's text.

kvkNumber.description: KvK (Chamber of Commerce) number of this administratie, when known.

loonheffingennummer.description: Loonheffingennummer of this administratie, when known -- distinct from `SettingsService::getDocumentsEmployerLoonheffingennummer()`, which is the single-tenant instance-wide fallback used before this change existed.

active.description: Whether this administratie is currently selectable in the switcher. An inactive administratie stays in the catalog (its child records keep their administrationId) but is not offered as a switch target.

abpAansluitingsplichtig.description: abp-aansluiting (REQ-ABP-001): whether this client administratie is legally obligated under the Wet Privatisering ABP (1996) to affiliate with ABP and file its pension-bearing payroll there. An admin-set determination only -- hrmq carries no employer-sector taxonomy today, so this is NEVER derived or computed from a sector, function, or CAO field; auto-derivation is a named fast-follow once such a taxonomy exists. Consumed by nl-abp-fund-required (lib/Standards/Checks/NlAbpChecks.php) to scope the completeness check to obligated administraties only.

AdministrationAccess.title: Administration access
AdministrationAccess.description: multi-administratie (design.md D2/D7): the accountant multi-client access model -- ONE membership row binding a Nextcloud user to an administratie with a role. An accountant user carries MANY rows (their whole client book); a single-company HR/employee user carries one. This is the closed set `AdministrationController::setActive` resolves the caller against (D4) and the switcher may offer (D5) -- a user can never activate an administratie with no row here. A plain declarative OpenRegister object (ADR-001 data-layer: domain data lives in the register), deliberately NOT a Nextcloud group -- an accountant's client book is app data, not an instance-admin concern.

userId.description: Denormalized Nextcloud user id (plain string, the app's existing userId/managerUserId link convention -- never a $ref, it names an account, not an Employee object).

administrationId.description: The Administration.administrationId business key this row grants access to. NOT a $ref (ADR-062 rule 7, the same convention every child schema's denormalized administrationId follows).

role.description: The caller's role on this administratie. `accountant`: one of potentially many client administraties on the caller's book. `hr`: the caller's single employer administratie. `employee`: the caller's own administratie, mirroring the app's existing @me self-service scope. Purely descriptive in the MVP -- the setter/switcher only check ROW PRESENCE, not this value (design.md D7); role-differentiated authorization is a named post-MVP fast-follow.
